distance_note: On Terry A. Francois Blvd, within the stretch DataSF's official 'Former San Francisco Redevelopment Agency Project Areas' boundary marks as Mission Bay South, and about 30m from Mission Bay South's own nearest tracked feature (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage/P24 waterfront lawn) -- versus roughly 470m from Mission Rock's own tracked footprint (Pier 48/50). Recorded as adjacent to Mission Bay, not Mission Rock, on that basis. Pier 54 itself predates and is not part of Mission Bay's OCII development program -- it is Port-jurisdiction maritime infrastructure.
summary: Pier 54, a Port-owned pier on Terry A. Francois Blvd, was condemned and closed in 2024 after years of structural deterioration, displacing the businesses that operated there. The Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31) budgets $2.0M to demolish the pier's shed; no funded timeline exists yet for removing the rest of the structure.

milestones.text: Pier 54 is officially red-tagged as unsafe.

Port sends Pier 54's tenants formal written notice of the pier's closure; its August 9, 2024 memo says the 11 tenants will need to vacate by the end of 2024. SFGate reported the closure in September 2024.

Port's draft Five-Year Capital Improvement Program (FY2027-31) budgets a "Pier 54 Shed Demolition" line item totaling $2.0M: $500,000 in FY2026-27 and $1,500,000 in FY2027-28. No line item for full substructure removal appears in the same document, and no source read says the demolition has started.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the closure-announcement milestone was dated December 2024, but the Port's August 9, 2024 memo says formal written notice went to tenants on July 15, 2024 and SFGate reported the closure in September 2024; it is now dated July 15, 2024. The February 2026 draft CIP milestone was flagged expected although the draft was published then; the flag was removed. Whether the shed demolition has started, and so whether 'being removed' is the right map status, is for the owner to confirm: no source read says it has.

That the Port planned to fence the pier to prevent vandalism is reported only in a search-engine summary of the SFGate article, not independently re-verified here against the full original article text (which sits behind a paywall; the mirror used for this record's other facts may not repeat that detail).

This record's site grouping ("Mission Bay South") reflects DataSF's official redevelopment-project-area boundary, which reaches this stretch of Terry A. Francois Blvd -- not a claim that Pier 54 is a Mission Bay OCII development block, which it is not.
